collections.title: 7-Pot
collections.description: A 7 Pot pepper hot sauce is characterized by extreme, immediate heat (900,000 to over 1.8 million Scoville Units) coupled with a surprisingly fruity, sweet, and slightly nutty flavor, often featuring a thick, savory profile. Named because one pod can spice seven pots of stew, these sauces offer a long-lasting, deep burn that frequently brings hints of garlic or earthiness behind the intense, sweat-inducing heat.

collections.title: Alcohol Infused
collections.description: Adding alcohol to hot sauce isn't just about the "buzz" (which usually cooks off anyway); it’s about chemistry . Alcohol acts as a solvent that extracts fat-soluble flavor compounds and heat from chili peppers that water or vinegar alone can't reach. It also adds complex sugars and acidity that can balance out a heavy dose of capsaicin.

collections.title: All Fruit Sauces
collections.description: Fruit has become a staple in the modern hot sauce landscape—think Mango Habanero, Pineapple Jalapeño, or even Blueberry Ghost Pepper. While it might seem like a trendy culinary gimmick, there is a deep scientific and sensory basis for why fruit and chili peppers are such a successful pairing. The primary reason people enjoy fruit in hot sauces is that the chemical components of fruit—specifically sugars and organic acids —directly mitigate the "pain" of capsaicin.

collections.title: Amarillo Peppers
collections.description: Commonly known as the Ají Amarillo , this vibrant orange pepper is the undisputed king of Peruvian cuisine. While many hot sauces rely on the smoky depth of chipotles or the face-melting heat of habaneros, Amarillo-based sauces offer a completely different profile: bright, fruity, and surprisingly complex.

collections.title: Ancho Pepper
collections.description: The Ancho chili is essentially the MVP of the Mexican pantry. If the jalapeño is the "famous one," the Ancho is the "respected one." It is deep, dark, and dependable, providing the foundational flavor for some of the most iconic dishes in Mexican cuisine.   Ancho chilis are very mild (1,000–1,500 Scoville units). Their natural sugars and earthy oils act as a "buffer," rounding out the sharp, stinging edge of super-hot peppers.

collections.title: Anchor Bar
collections.description: Anchor Bar is the world-renowned "Home of the Original Buffalo Wing." Established in 1935 by Frank and Teressa Bellissimo, it transitioned from a local Italian-American neighborhood bar to a global culinary destination after a single late-night snack in 1964. In 2003, the James Beard Foundation honored the Anchor Bar with its "America’s Classics" award. We carry all of their hot sauces from mild to extreme heat.  Anchor Bar sauces are known for being sharp, vinegary, and buttery . They do not use complex fruity or smoky notes; they are purely traditional.

collections.title: Apollo Pepper
collections.description: If you’re a fan of heat that feels less like a snack and more like a religious experience, meet the Apollo Pepper . Bred by the legendary Ed Currie of PuckerButt Pepper Company—the same mastermind behind the Carolina Reaper and Pepper X—the Apollo is a cross-breed of its two famous predecessors. It’s a botanical powerhouse designed for one specific purpose: to push the limits of human capsaicin tolerance. Unlike many superhots that provide a slow, building burn, the Apollo is known for an instant, aggressive heat that targets the entire mouth and throat simultaneously. While official lab results vary, the Apollo is estimated to hover around 2.5 to 3 million Scoville Heat Units (SHU).

collections.title: Apples
collections.description: While exotic fruits like mango or pineapple often get the spotlight, apples are the "quiet architects" of the hot sauce world. They are rarely the star of the label, but they are frequently the secret ingredient that transforms a sharp, watery sauce into a professional-grade condiment.

collections.title: As Seen On Hot Ones
collections.description: Starting out on YouTube as just a small show, Hot Ones has turned into a YouTube sensation for over 10 years now, helping the hot sauce industry boom. Check out some of the sauces that have been seen on the Hot Ones show over the years. They are mild to extra hot.

collections.title: Ashley Food
collections.description: Ashley Food Company (commonly known by its flagship brand, Mad Dog 357 ) is a legendary Massachusetts-based company that helped pioneer the "extreme heat" category of the hot sauce world. Founded in 1991 by David Ashley , the brand is famous for pushing the limits of the Scoville scale while maintaining a surprisingly high standard for culinary quality. Ashley Food is best known for the Mad Dog 357 line. They are the industry leaders in pepper extracts (essentially liquid capsaicin). These are not meant to be used like traditional hot sauce but rather as food additives.

collections.title: Bacon Flavored Sauces
collections.description: Bacon-flavored hot sauces combine the rich, smoky, and salty savoriness of cured pork belly with the tangy, spicy, and sharp kick of chili peppers. Designed for breakfast foods, burgers, and BBQ, these sauces often achieve their savory depth through natural smoke flavoring and yeast extracts, offering a high-umami, savory experience ranging from mild cayenne to extreme, scorching heat.

collections.title: BBQ Sauce and Marinades
collections.description: If hot sauce is the lightning bolt that strikes your palate, then BBQ sauces and marinades are the rolling thunder that follows—deep, resonant, and essential to the experience. While a few drops of reaper sauce can provide that instant adrenaline rush, the real magic of outdoor cooking happens when heat meets soul. Whether you’re slow-smoking a brisket for twelve hours or quick-searing wings on a Tuesday night, the liquid you choose dictates the story your meal tells.

collections.title: Bell Peppers
collections.description: The Bell Pepper is the ultimate "utility player" in the hot sauce world. It might seem strange to put a zero-heat pepper in a hot sauce, but for professional sauce makers, the bell pepper is an essential tool for balancing flavor, texture, and intensity. Bell peppers allow a maker to "bulk up" a sauce while keeping the heat levels under control.

collections.title: Bello Signature
collections.description: Bello Signature is an artisanal condiment brand that is deeply rooted in the  Buffalo, New York food scene. It is best known for its Bello Signature Wing Sauce , which has earned a "hidden gem" status among Western New York wing purists who want a step up from standard commercial glazes. The brand was developed to mimic the exact consistency and "clinging" power of sauces used in high-end Buffalo wing joints. Unlike mass-produced brands that can taste "metallic" due to high preservative counts, Bello focuses on a cleaner, more vibrant flavor profile. It is often grouped with brands like Murph's or Lucky Snipe as part of the "Next Generation" of Buffalo condiments—brands that respect the 1964 origins of the wing but are trying to elevate the ingredients for a modern palate.

collections.title: Best Sellers
collections.description: Welcome to our Best Sellers collection—the reigning champions of heat, flavor, and culinary obsession.  If you’re looking for the absolute crowd-pleasers that keep hot sauce fanatics coming back for more, you’ve arrived at the right place. Whether you are a seasoned chili head looking for your next high-Scoville challenge or a flavor-first foodie seeking the perfect balance of sweet and heat, these are our community's top-rated, most-wanted bottles. Explore the bottles that everyone is talking about, find a definitive favorite, and elevate your next meal.

collections.title: Big Red's Hot Sauce
collections.description: Big Red’s Hot Sauce is a prominent, family-owned craft sauce company based in Phoenix, Arizona . Founded in 2011 by Paul "Big Red" Ford and his wife Tasia , the brand is celebrated for its "Flavor Tour" philosophy—an approach that prioritizes complex, culinary-focused flavor profiles over simple, destructive heat. Big Red’s sauces are known for their thick, chunky textures and unique ingredient combinations that reflect the desert Southwest and Paul Ford’s personal journey.

collections.title: Black Cherries
collections.description: When you think of fruit in hot sauce, your mind likely jumps to the tropical sting of mango or the bright acidity of pineapple. However, black cherries offer a sophisticated, dark-horse alternative that transforms a simple condiment into a gourmet experience. Unlike their brighter cousins, black cherries bring a deep, "jammy" sweetness and a hint of earthy tartness that pairs exceptionally well with smoked peppers and heavy spices.

collections.title: Black Garlic
collections.description: If you’re looking to level up your spice game, black garlic hot sauce is the ultimate "cheat code." While traditional hot sauces usually rely on the sharp bite of vinegar and the raw sting of peppers, black garlic sauces play a much more sophisticated game.  The magic of black garlic in a hot sauce is its ability to provide umami —that "fifth taste" that makes your mouth water. It acts as a bridge between the intense heat of the peppers and the brightness of the vinegar.

collections.title: Blackberries
collections.description: When most people think of hot sauce, they picture bright reds and oranges—the colors of fire and vinegar. But there is a dark, sophisticated side to the Scoville scale that belongs entirely to the blackberry . Integrating blackberries into a hot sauce isn't just about adding sweetness; it’s about depth. They offer a complex profile of tartness, earthy tannins, and a deep purple hue that transforms a standard condiment into a gourmet glaze.

collections.title: Blair's Death
collections.description: Blair’s Death Sauce is one of the most legendary and influential brands in the history of the hot sauce industry. Founded by Blair Lazar in the early 1990s, the company is credited with pioneering the "extreme heat" movement and the collector's market for ultra-hot condiments. What started as a way for a bartender to get rowdy patrons to leave the bar at closing time eventually became a global phenomenon known for its iconic "Skull" keychains and record-breaking heat levels.  Blair Lazar’s philosophy has always been centered on pushing the boundaries of what the human palate can endure.

collections.title: Blonde Beard's
collections.description: Blonde Beard’s is a family-owned craft sauce brand from Denver, Colorado, founded by Adam and Cara Nelson. They are famous for creating the world’s first "craft Buffalo sauce" line, moving away from conventional oil-based wing sauces to focus on gourmet, small-batch ingredients. The brand is most notably known for using real butter in their bottled sauces. While most commercial wing sauces use hydrogenated oils to mimic a buttery taste, Blonde Beard's uses real dairy, giving their sauces a signature thick, rich, and creamy consistency that clings to food.

collections.title: Blueberries
collections.description: Blueberry hot sauces are the dark horses of the condiment world. While the idea of mixing a breakfast staple with fiery peppers might sound like a culinary dare, it’s actually a masterclass in flavor balancing . The natural acidity and deep sweetness of blueberries provide a perfect counterpoint to the sharp, aggressive heat of super-hot peppers. Unlike refined sugar, blueberry sweetness is earthy. It tames the "burn" of the pepper without making the sauce taste like candy. They provide a bright tang that complements vinegar, helping to lift the heavier notes of peppers like Habaneros or Ghosts.

collections.title: Bootsie's Sauce Co
collections.description: Bootsie's Sauce Co. is a craft condiment brand based in Delray Beach, Florida , founded on the principle of bringing "low and slow" Southern culinary traditions to the hot sauce world. Named after the founder's grandmother, the brand focuses on complex, multi-layered flavors that act more like a concentrated culinary base than a simple table sauce. They are widely recognized for their thick, rich textures and their ability to blend savory, smoky, and sweet elements into a balanced, soul-food inspired heat experience.

collections.title: Bourbon
collections.description: When you think of bourbon, your mind probably goes straight to a crystal tumbler or a slow-sipping cocktail. But in the world of craft hot sauces, bourbon is much more than a drink—it’s a flavor powerhouse that bridges the gap between blistering heat and culinary complexity. Adding bourbon to a hot sauce isn't just about the "booze factor" (most of the alcohol cooks off, anyway); it’s about the unique chemistry that happens when charred oak meets chili peppers.

collections.title: Bourbon Country
collections.description: Bourbon Country is a specialty condiment brand that focuses on the intersection of two quintessential Southern traditions: aged Kentucky bourbon and fiery chili peppers. The company is built on a "spirit-infused" culinary philosophy, where the complex, oaky notes of bourbon are used to soften and enhance the heat of the sauce. It is a brand that prioritizes depth, barrel-aged character, and a sophisticated sweetness over raw, aggressive spice.

collections.title: Bravado
collections.description: Bravado Spice Co. is a Houston-based artisanal sauce company founded by James Nelson and Jeremiah Tallerine. Since its inception, the brand has carved out a unique space in the hot sauce world by focusing on "culinary-first" profiles that prioritize complex flavor combinations over sheer heat. They are widely recognized for their bold experimentation, often blending super-hot peppers with unexpected fruits and savory aromatics.  The company’s mission is centered on the idea that hot sauce should be a gourmet ingredient rather than just a way to add heat.

collections.title: Brooks' House of Bar-B-Q
collections.description: Brooks’ House of BBQ is a landmark institution in the world of American barbecue, specifically representing the unique "Empire State" style of slow-cooked poultry and meats. Based in Oneonta, New York , the company began as a family poultry farm in the early 1950s and evolved into a massive destination restaurant and bottling operation.  Their entry into the spicy market follows the "food-first" philosophy. It is typically a vinegar-based hot sauce that utilizes peppers to provide a sharp, clean sting that complements the smoky flavors of grilled meat without masking the flavor of the charcoal.

collections.title: Brown Sugar
collections.description: There is something nearly poetic about the marriage of fire and molasses. While many hot sauces focus on the sharp, acidic sting of vinegar, brown sugar hot sauces play a different game. They lean into the "sweet heat" profile, where the deep, caramel notes of the sugar act as a buffer for the pepper’s capsaicin. In the world of Scoville units, sugar is the ultimate peacemaker. Brown sugar, specifically, brings more to the table than white sugar because of its molasses content .

collections.title: Bunsters
collections.description: Bunsters is an Australian hot sauce company that gained international fame (and notoriety) for its provocative branding, high-quality ingredients, and viral success. Based in Perth, Western Australia, the brand was founded by former journalist Renae Bunster . The company began in 2011 after Renae Bunster returned from a trip to Central America. What started as a hobby for friends quickly turned into a global business when her flagship sauce, "Shit the Bed," went viral in 2015. The name was originally a joke between friends, but it became the hook that launched the brand into the global spotlight.

collections.title: Burning Asphalt Enterprises LLC
collections.description: Burning Asphalt LLC is a specialty condiment company based in Buffalo, New York , that has built a cult following by merging "gearhead" car culture with high-intensity heat. Founded by Jerry "The Sauce Man" Santora , the brand is designed for people who love the smell of burning rubber almost as much as the sting of a ghost pepper. It is a brand that leans heavily into a high-octane, "asphalt-tough" aesthetic, using automotive-themed names and packaging to stand out in the crowded hot sauce market. While they are famous for their "extreme" offerings, Jerry Santora emphasizes that the "Asphalt" experience is about flavor first. Even their hottest sauces are built on a foundation of savory aromatics like garlic, onion, and various vinegars to ensure they actually enhance food.

collections.title: Butternut Squash
collections.description: When you think of hot sauce, your mind probably goes straight to the sharp sting of vinegar or the fruity punch of habaneros. But there’s a secret weapon in the world of craft condiments that’s changing the game: Butternut Squash . While it might seem more at home in a Thanksgiving soup than a hot sauce bottle, butternut squash is a culinary powerhouse for balancing heat. Its naturally sweet, nutty profile provides a sophisticated backdrop that does more than just add flavor—it transforms the entire structure of the sauce.

collections.title: CaJohn's
collections.description: CaJohns Fiery Foods is one of the most decorated and respected names in the hot sauce industry. Founded in 1996 by John "CaJohn" Hard , the company is a pioneer of the "craft" hot sauce movement, famous for moving beyond simple vinegar-based sauces to create complex, gourmet flavor profiles. Based in Columbus, Ohio , CaJohns has won hundreds of industry awards and was one of the first companies to focus on the unique characteristics of specific pepper varietals.  Hard’s culinary background drove the company to create sauces that enhanced food. Even at their highest heat levels, CaJohns sauces are known for having a distinct, delicious taste profile rather than just chemical heat.

collections.title: Cantina Royal Hot Sauce
collections.description: Cantina Royal is a vibrant, chef-driven hot sauce brand born out of the kitchen of the eponymous Mexican restaurant in Williamsburg, Brooklyn . Founded by Diana Kuan and Chef Julio Mina , the brand is celebrated for its deep roots in traditional Mexican flavors, reimagined with a modern, "New York" culinary edge. Unlike brands that rely on vinegar to carry the heat, Cantina Royal focuses on complexity, texture, and the "soul" of the chili pepper . Cantina Royal reached international fame when Tomasa was featured on Season 11 of Hot Ones . Host Sean Evans and guests frequently praised it for its incredible depth of flavor. They are respected for their "Zero-Extract" policy—even their hotter sauces rely entirely on the natural potency of the chili pods.

collections.title: Carolina Reaper
collections.description: Carolina Reaper  is one the "heavy metal" peppers of the pepper world. Bred by Ed Currie of PuckerButt Pepper Company, it held the Guinness World Record for the hottest chili in the world for a decade ( roughly 1.6 to 2.2 million Scoville Heat Units ) . When you are dealing with a Reaper, you aren't just making a sauce; you are managing a chemical reaction. Most people expect the Reaper to taste like battery acid, but it is actually a descendant of the Habanero family.

collections.title: Carrots
collections.description: While peppers provide the heat, carrots are the unsung heroes of the hot sauce world. If a pepper is the lead guitarist, the carrot is the bassist—providing the necessary structure, body, and rhythm that keeps the whole performance from falling apart.  Carrots are high in fiber and pectin. When cooked down and blended, they create a smooth, velvety emulsion . Instead of dumping processed white sugar into a mash, craft sauce makers use carrots to provide a natural, earthy sweetness . This helps balance the aggressive acidity of vinegar and the sharp "bite" of capsaicin without making the sauce taste like candy.

collections.title: Cayenne Pepper
collections.description: The Cayenne pepper is the "Original" of the hot sauce world. While other chilies compete for the title of smokiest or hottest, the Cayenne is the reliable, sharp, and clean-hitting pepper that defined the entire Louisiana-style sauce and wing sauce movement. It doesn't hide behind complex fruity or floral notes—it just delivers a straight-to-the-point, peppery sting. Measuring between 30,000 and 50,000 Scoville Heat Units , it is the definition of "medium-hot." It’s spicy enough to make its presence known but approachable enough for everyday use.

collections.title: Cherries
collections.description: When you think of hot sauce, your mind likely jumps to vinegar, garlic, and tongue-scorching peppers. However, the addition of cherries transforms a standard condiment into a sophisticated, multi-layered glaze. Cherry-based hot sauces occupy that perfect "sweet-and-heat" niche, leveraging the fruit's natural acidity and deep sugars to balance the aggressive bite of capsaicin.

collections.title: Chile De Arbol
collections.description: The Chile de Árbol (translated as "tree chili") is the elegant, slender powerhouse of the Mexican pantry. While it may look delicate, it is the primary source of the "electric" heat found in the best street taco sauces. It doesn't offer the dark, heavy sweetness of some dried chilies; instead, it provides a clean, sharp, and nutty bite that cuts through the richness of any meal.

collections.title: Chili Oil and Chili Crisp
collections.description: Traditional hot sauces are fantastic for adding bright acidity and sharp heat. Chili crisp and chili oil do something completely different. While traditional hot sauces rely on vinegar and sharp heat, chili crisp brings a completely different sensory experience to the table: The Addictive Crunch: Packed with fried garlic, shallots, and toasted chili flakes, it adds a loud, textured bite that standard hot sauces just can't match. The Umami Bomb: The oil extracts deep, savory flavor from the peppers rather than just raw heat, often boosted by rich ingredients like mushroom powder or fried beans. Insane Versatility: Without a heavy vinegar base, it elevates food without masking it. It works perfectly on everything from noodles and pizza to eggs and even vanilla ice cream.

collections.title: Chipotle Peppers
collections.description: In the hot sauce world, the Chipotle is the undisputed king of gravity. While other chilis provide high-frequency heat and sharp stings, the Chipotle provides a deep, resonant "bass note" that anchors the entire bottle. It transforms a sauce from a mere condiment into a rich, savory experience.

collections.title: Clearance Items
collections.description: Our flavor hunt never stops. To make room on our digital shelves for our next round of curated, small-batch discoveries, we’re opening up the vault for a limited-time rotation. These aren't leftovers—they are top-tier, artisan hot sauces from incredible makers that we personally vetted, loved, and brought in for you. Think of it as a final-chance victory lap for some of our absolute favorite heat profiles, now at an unbeatable price. Snag these premium bottles to elevate your pantry before they’re gone for good!

collections.title: Coffee
collections.description: Mixing coffee and hot sauce might sound like a caffeine-induced fever dream, but it is actually a masterclass in flavor balancing. The bitterness of a dark roast acts as a perfect foil to the sharp acidity of vinegar and the searing heat of peppers. Think of it like a savory mole sauce or a Texas-style dry rub —but in a bottle.

collections.title: Cooking with Peppers
collections.description:
In the culinary world, peppers are less about "surviving the heat" and more about balancing sweetness, acidity, and earthiness. When you move away from the extreme super-hots, you find peppers that actually serve as the backbone of global cuisines.

 Here is a comprehensive guide to pepper varieties, their heat levels, and technical cooking applications.

 Mild and Sweet Peppers (0 to 2,500 SHU)

 Bell Pepper (0 SHU) How to Cook: Use high heat to caramelize the high water content. Roasting whole until charred allows you to steam and peel the skin, resulting in a buttery, soft texture. For a "trinity" base in stews, sauté finely diced pieces with onion and celery. Detailed Pairings: Proteins: Italian sausage, ground turkey, and white-fleshed fish. Produce: Red onion, garlic, and eggplant. Flavor Enhancers: Fresh basil, balsamic glaze, and salty cheeses like feta or halloumi.

 Poblano (1,000 to 1,500 SHU) How to Cook: The skin is tough, so roasting and peeling is standard. Slice the roasted flesh into "rajas" (strips) and sauté with heavy cream and onions for a classic side. They are the ideal vessel for stuffing with cheese or grains because their walls are structurally sound. Detailed Pairings: Dairy: Mexican crema, Oaxaca cheese, and goat cheese. Grains: Corn and toasted quinoa. Spices: Cumin and dried oregano.

 Anaheim (500 to 2,500 SHU) How to Cook: Best used in slow-cooking or grilling. Toss them whole onto a grill until blistered, then chop them into a salsa verde. They hold up well in slow-cooker pork stews (Chile Verde), where they provide a subtle vegetal background. Detailed Pairings: Proteins: Pork shoulder and eggs. Produce: Tomatillos and zucchini. Acids: Apple cider vinegar and lime.

 Medium Heat Peppers (2,500 to 30,000 SHU)

 Jalapeño (2,500 to 8,000 SHU) How to Cook: For maximum flavor with less heat, remove the pith and seeds. Quick-pickling in a 1:1 ratio of vinegar and water with salt and sugar preserves their crunch. If roasting, keep them whole to concentrate the oils. Detailed Pairings: Fats: Bacon, cream cheese, and avocado. Fruit: Peach, pineapple, and mango (for fresh salsas). Herbs: Fresh cilantro and scallions.

 Serrano (10,000 to 23,000 SHU) How to Cook: Since the skin is much thinner than a jalapeño, you don't need to peel them. Mince them raw for a bright, aggressive heat in ceviche or guacamole. You can also flash-fry them whole in hot oil for 30 seconds to serve as a blistered garnish. Detailed Pairings: Seafood: Shrimp, scallops, and white fish. Produce: Radish and tomato. Aromatics: Ginger and lemongrass.

 Guajillo (Dried) (2,500 to 5,000 SHU) How to Cook: You must toast these in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side until they become fragrant and pliable. After toasting, submerge them in boiling water for 15 minutes. Blend the rehydrated pods with garlic to create a rich, red base for marinades or birria. Detailed Pairings: Proteins: Beef chuck, brisket, and lamb. Earthy Spices: Cinnamon, cloves, and toasted pumpkin seeds (pepitas).

 Hot Peppers (30,000 to 350,000 SHU)

 Cayenne (30,000 to 50,000 SHU) How to Cook: Most commonly used in its dried, powdered form. Use it in dry rubs for meats or whisk it into vinegar-based sauces. If using fresh, mince very finely to ensure even distribution, as the heat is sharp and concentrated. Detailed Pairings: Fried Foods: Fried chicken and tempura. Acid: Lemon juice and cider vinegar. Sweet: Maple syrup or honey.

 Thai Bird’s Eye (50,000 to 100,000 SHU) How to Cook: Lightly bruise the peppers with the flat of a knife before tossing them into a stir-fry or soup; this releases the spicy oils without making the dish impossible to eat. You can also infuse them into peanut or vegetable oil for a shelf-stable chili oil. Detailed Pairings: Umami: Fish sauce, soy sauce, and shrimp paste. Aromatics: Thai basil, garlic, and shallots. Creamy: Coconut milk and peanut butter.

 Habanero (100,000 to 350,000 SHU) How to Cook: These have a distinct floral and apricot-like aroma. To preserve this, blend them raw into fruit-based glazes or ferment them with salt and water for two weeks to create a complex hot sauce. Use gloves when handling to avoid skin burns. Detailed Pairings: Fruit: Mango, passionfruit, and apricot. Sweeteners: Agave nectar and honey. Spices: Allspice and nutmeg (common in Jerk seasoning).

 Super Hot Peppers (1,000,000+ SHU)

 Ghost Pepper (Bhut Jolokia) (1,000,000+ SHU) How to Cook: Use the "infusion" method. Poke a single hole in a pepper and drop it into a large pot of chili or stew for only 10 to 15 minutes, then discard. This provides the heat and smoke without the danger of someone eating a whole piece. Detailed Pairings: Bold Flavors: Smoked meats, molasses, and dark chocolate. Starch: Heavy potatoes and bread.

 Carolina Reaper (2,200,000+ SHU) How to Cook: Generally too hot for standard cooking. The best application is dehydrating the peppers and grinding them into a fine dust. Use a toothpick to add a microscopic amount of this dust to a dish to increase the "scorch" without altering the flavor profile. Detailed Pairings: Proteins: Very fatty BBQ meats like pork belly or brisket that can stand up to the extreme capsaicin.

 Essential Cooking Techniques

 Heat Control: The capsaicin is concentrated in the white pith (placenta), not the seeds themselves. Scraping out the pith with a spoon is the most effective way to lower the SHU.

 Safety Protocols: When working with anything hotter than a Serrano, wear nitrile gloves. If you get "chili burn" on your skin, do not use water; use milk, yogurt, or vegetable oil to dissolve the capsaicin.

 The Vapor Factor: Never throw hot peppers into a dry, scorching hot pan. The capsaicin will aerosolize and act like pepper spray in your kitchen. Always ensure there is a layer of oil or liquid in the pan first.

collections.title: Dates
collections.description: Stinging vinegar, sharp salt, and the searing heat of capsaicin are most likely what people think about when thinking of hot sauces. However, the secret weapon of the world’s most balanced sauces isn't a pepper at all—it's the date . As the craft hot sauce movement has evolved, makers have moved away from refined sugars, looking instead to whole fruits to provide depth. Dates have emerged as the "MVP" of natural sweeteners, offering much more than just a sugary kick.

collections.title: Datil Pepper
collections.description: The influence of the Datil Pepper in the world of hot sauces is defined by its geographical rarity and its unusual ability to balance high intensity with natural sweetness. Unlike many sauces that focus on sharp acidity or pure heat, Datil-based sauces prioritize a "sweet heat" profile that has shaped the culinary identity of Northeast Florida for centuries. 100,000-300,000 SHU provides a significant but manageable kick.

collections.title: Down To Ferment
collections.description: Down To Ferment (often abbreviated as DTF ) is an independent, craft hot sauce company based out of San Diego, California. Founded by industry veterans Sean Kirkpatrick (a professional chef) and Ryan (a mixologist and U.S. Marine Corps veteran), the brand has carved out a distinct niche in the highly competitive hot sauce scene by focusing on a "flavor first, heat second" philosophy. While 99% of hot sauces on the market rely on white or apple cider vinegar to preserve the sauce and add tang, Down To Ferment uses house-brewed kombucha instead.

collections.title: Dragon's Breath Pepper
collections.description: The Dragon's Breath pepper is less of a culinary ingredient and more of a biological event. Bred in Wales by Mike Smith in collaboration with Nottingham Trent University, it was initially developed not for the dinner table, but for potential use as a topical anesthetic for people allergic to traditional numbing agents.  It has a staggering  2.48 million Scoville Heat Units (SHU) and it technically surpasses the intensity of the former world record holder, the Carolina Reaper, making it one of the most volatile substances in the plant kingdom.

collections.title: Duff's
collections.description: Duff’s Famous Wings is a legendary pillar of the Buffalo, New York, wing scene. Since first serving wings in 1969 , Duff's has become famous for its "the hotter the better" philosophy, eventually bottling their sauces to allow fans to recreate the experience at home .  In the hot sauce community, Duff's is respected for its consistency. While many brands try to reinvent the wheel with exotic ingredients, Duff's is celebrated for perfecting the original 1960s Buffalo formula. It is widely considered one of the few bottled sauces that actually tastes "restaurant-quality" when used at home.

collections.title: Elijah's Extreme Gourmet Sauces
collections.description: Elijah’s Extreme is a father-and-son-owned specialty hot sauce company based in Gastonia, North Carolina . Founded in 2014 by Elijah and Croix Morey , the brand started with a simple garden project when Elijah was only six years old and evolved into a globally recognized name in the "Super-Hot" category. They are celebrated for their ability to take the world's hottest peppers—like the Carolina Reaper and Trinidad Scorpion —and balance them with gourmet flavors like black cherries, bourbon, and roasted garlic. Elijah’s Extreme is a dominant force in the competition circuit, having won over 60 industry awards , including multiple first-place finishes at the NYC Hot Sauce Expo , Scovie Awards , and ZestFest . They are widely respected by "Chili-heads" for their honesty; if the label says "Extreme," the heat is guaranteed to be there.

collections.title: Extra Hot Sauces
collections.description: For those who find standard "hot" sauces underwhelming, our Extra Hot lineup offers the next level of intensity. Expect a searing, long-lasting heat that pushes your limits. While these sauces provide a serious kick, they still maintain the integrity of their ingredients, offering a complex fire that pairs perfectly with bold dishes.

collections.title: Extract Sauces
collections.description: Welcome to the danger zone of the hot sauce world: Extract Hot Sauces . These aren't your average, everyday condiments meant for casual splashing; these are mad-scientist creations fueled by pure, laboratory-grade capsaicin extract. Engineered for seasoned heat-seekers and ultimate chiliheads, extract sauces bypass the pleasant warmth of standard peppers to deliver an immediate, uncompromising explosion of scorching heat. If you are looking to test your limits, elevate your culinary daredevilry, or add a drop of pure fire to a massive pot of chili, you’ve arrived at the right place.

collections.title: Facepunch Hot Sauces
collections.description: Facepunch Foods is a small-batch producer that focuses on flavor-forward hot sauces. Unlike brands that aim to melt your face off with pure capsaicin, they lean into the natural sweetness, acidity, and earthiness of various peppers. Because they focus on small batches, the quality of the pepper mash is usually higher than mass-produced grocery store brands. They often partner with local businesses and restaurants to create custom blends, making them a staple in their local culinary scene.

collections.title: Fat Cat Gourmet
collections.description: Fat Cat Gourmet (officially Fat Cat Foods) is a multi-award-winning specialty food company based in Orlando, Florida . Founded in 2010 by husband-and-wife team Eyal Goldshmid and Deborah Moskowitz , the brand was born out of a desire to create "exotic" condiments that bridge the gap between high-end culinary glazes and traditional hot sauces. They are widely recognized for their vibrant, fruit-forward profiles and their commitment to using all-natural, preservative-free ingredients . Fat Cat is a heavyweight in the "Fiery Foods" award circuit.

collections.title: Figueroa Brothers
collections.description: The Figueroa Brothers (specifically David and Greg Figueroa) are legendary figures in the hot sauce industry, widely recognized for transforming the way "gourmet" hot sauce is marketed and consumed in the United States. Based in New Orleans , they are the founders of Figueroa Brothers, Inc. Their identity is built on  rebellion and intensity . Long before "super-hots" like the Carolina Reaper existed, they were pushing the boundaries of what was considered edible. They popularized the use of warnings on labels, claiming the sauce was "too hot to handle," which served as an irresistible challenge to chili-heads. These sauces almost always utilize pepper extract (oleoresin capsicum) . This provides an immediate, searing heat that hits the tongue like a needle. It lacks the "slow build" of natural super-hots and focuses on a sharp, aggressive sting.

collections.title: Florida Man's Lunacy
collections.description: Florida Man’s Lunacy is a bold, high-octane hot sauce brand that leans into the viral "Florida Man" internet phenomenon, celebrating the wild, unpredictable, and often chaotic energy of the Sunshine State. Beyond the humorous branding, the sauce is known for its tropical, citrus-heavy profile and a heat level that is surprisingly formidable. It is a medium-to-thick, pulpy sauce that prioritizes a "bright and biting" experience, designed to complement the seafood and outdoor lifestyle of the Southeast. The burn is radiant and lingering. It starts with a pleasant fruity sweetness on the tip of the tongue before the Reaper heat begins to build in the back of the throat—a sensation that fans of the brand describe as "the sun coming up."

collections.title: Freelance Foods
collections.description: Freelance Foods is a craft hot sauce company based in Buffalo, New York , that focuses on small-batch, artisanal flavors. In a region dominated by the classic "Cayenne and Vinegar" Buffalo wing style, Freelance Foods stands out by creating more complex, multi-layered sauces that appeal to "flavor-chasers" as much as "heat-seekers." The name "Freelance Foods" reflects the brand's independent, creative spirit. They don't follow the traditional rules of hot sauce manufacturing; instead, they treat each recipe like a culinary experiment. Every bottle is produced in limited quantities, allowing for greater control over the freshness of the produce and the balance of the spices.

collections.title: Garlic
collections.description: In the realm of sauces and rubs, garlic is the "flavor anchor." It provides the deep, resonant base notes that allow the high notes of vinegar and the fire of the peppers to shine without feeling hollow. In a hot sauce, garlic does more than just add flavor—it changes the way your tongue perceives the heat. BBQ sauce is often a battle between extreme sweetness and sharp acidity. Garlic acts as the peacemaker. In the world of barbecue, the most legendary base for any rub is SPG (Salt, Pepper, Garlic).

collections.title: Ghost Pepper
collections.description: The Ghost Pepper (Bhut Jolokia) is the legendary "slow creeper" of the chili world. While it lost its world-record title years ago, it remains the most popular super-hot for sauce makers because it has a distinct, earthy personality that isn't just about raw pain. The Ghost Pepper is famous for its delayed onset . Unlike some peppers that sting the tip of your tongue immediately, the Ghost Pepper has a "slow fuse." At over 1,000,000 Scoville Units , you’ll taste the sauce, notice the flavor, and then—about 15 to 30 seconds later—the heat begins to bloom in the back of the throat.

collections.title: Ginger Goat
collections.description: The company was founded by Guy DuPlantier , a hot sauce enthusiast who began experimenting with recipes in his home kitchen. The name "Ginger Goat" is a nod to DuPlantier’s own red hair and a lighthearted take on the "GOAT" (Greatest of All Time) acronym. Unlike many brands that focus solely on "brutal" heat, DuPlantier’s philosophy centered on balance . The major turning point for Ginger Goat came in 2021 . Their sauce was selected to be featured on Season 15 of the massive YouTube hit  Hot Ones .

collections.title: Gluten Free
collections.description: Enjoy the fire with total peace of mind in our Gluten-Free collection . We’ve vetted every hot sauce, BBQ glaze, and dry rub to ensure they are strictly free of wheat, barley, rye, and hidden thickeners. Whether managing a sensitivity or Celiac disease, you can explore everything from mild blends to super-hot reapers with 100% gourmet taste and transparent labeling.

collections.title: Habanero Pepper
collections.description: For decades, the Habanero was the world-record holder for heat. While "Superhots" like the Carolina Reaper have since surpassed it in raw numbers, the Habanero remains the gold standard for sauce makers because it hits a perfect biological "sweet spot" where intense heat meets incredible flavor.

collections.title: Hank Sauce
collections.description: Hank Sauce is a premier craft hot sauce brand based in Sea Isle City, New Jersey . Founded in 2011 by college roommates Hank Porter, Josh "Mouse" McLinden, and Matt "Beamer" Pittaluga , the brand has grown from a local boardwalk favorite into a nationally recognized name in the specialty food world. The brand is famous for its "Flavor First" philosophy, which moves away from the aggressive, vinegar-heavy style of traditional hot sauces toward a more sophisticated, "sauce-like" consistency. Hank Sauce is thicker than a standard hot sauce but thinner than a BBQ sauce. It "clings" beautifully to food without making it soggy.

collections.title: Hatch Chili Peppers
collections.description: Hatch Chile peppers are the crown jewels of New Mexico’s culinary scene, specifically grown in the mineral-rich soil of the Hatch Valley. Unlike generic green chilies, Hatch peppers are prized for their terroir —the unique environment gives them a distinct smoky, buttery, and earthy flavor that intensifies when roasted.

collections.title: Heatonist
collections.description: HEATONIST is arguably the most influential retail force in the modern hot sauce industry. Founded in 2013 by Noah Chaimberg and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York , it transformed hot sauce from a niche "dare" commodity into a gourmet culinary movement. HEATONIST is not just a store; it is a curator, a collaborator, and the official sauce partner for the viral YouTube sensation Hot Ones . HEATONIST famously refuses to sell any sauce that uses capsaicin extracts. They believe that heat should come naturally from the peppers themselves, ensuring a cleaner burn and better flavor profile.

collections.title: Hell Fire Detroit
collections.description: Hell Fire Detroit is a high-end, artisan hot sauce company based in Detroit, Michigan . Founded by Donre’ Walker in 2015 , the brand is built on a "farm-to-bottle" philosophy that highlights the pure, unadulterated flavor of specific chili peppers. Unlike many brands that blend multiple ingredients, Hell Fire Detroit focuses on simplicity , usually featuring only 4 to 5 ingredients per bottle. The brand’s identity is centered on minimalism and transparency . They don't use thickeners, gums, or artificial preservatives. While they use apple cider vinegar for stability, it is never the dominant flavor. The pepper is always the protagonist. Because the peppers are roasted, you will see small black flecks of charred skin in the sauce. This provides a "fire-grilled" aroma that is the brand's signature.

collections.title: Hell's Kitchen Hot Sauce
collections.description: Founded in 2014 by Ron Menin , this brand is the quintessential "indie" success story of the hot sauce world.  Having worked in fine dining, Menin hated "stunt sauces" that only offered pain. His mission was to create a "culinary" hot sauce—one that uses the pepper’s heat as a vehicle for the fruit and spice notes, not just a way to ruin a meal.

collections.title: Hellfire Hot Sauce
collections.description: Hellfire Hot Sauce is a premier "ultra-premium" sauce manufacturer based in Lake Geneva, Wisconsin . Founded in 2009 by Diana and Merle "The Hellfire" Metzler , the brand has become one of the most respected and decorated names in the industry. They are famous for their "Extreme" branding—featuring intricate, dark, and often supernatural artwork—and for producing some of the hottest natural sauces (no extracts) in the world. The Hellfire identity is built on the belief that heat should never sacrifice flavor . While they produce sauces that can challenge even the most seasoned "chili-heads," they are known for their sophisticated culinary foundations. Hellfire is one of the most winning brands in history. They are viewed as the "Elite" tier of the hot sauce world—the brand you buy when you want to experience the absolute limit of what natural peppers can do.

collections.title: High Desert Sauce Co
collections.description: High Desert Sauce Co. is an artisanal, small-batch craft hot sauce company based out of Tucson, Arizona . Established around 2018, the brand has built a stellar reputation in the hot sauce community for creating complex, culinary-forward profiles that lean heavily on regional Southwestern ingredients and fire-roasted pepper bases. Their core philosophy focuses on balancing bold heat with fresh, natural flavor, completely avoiding artificial preservatives, processed sugars, and thickening agents.

collections.title: High River Sauces
collections.description: High River Sauces is a premier "rock 'n' roll" hot sauce brand that sits at the intersection of heavy metal culture and high-end culinary arts. Founded in 2011 by Steve Seabury —a music industry veteran, cookbook author, and dedicated "chili-head"—the brand has become one of the most respected names in the craft sauce movement. Based in New York , High River is famous for its bold, "in-your-face" flavors and its pivotal role in organizing major industry events like the NYC Hot Sauce Expo . A bottle of High River is generally characterized by "Vibrant Acidity and Fruit Forwardness". High River is one of the most decorated brands in the world, consistently winning Scovie Awards , Golden Chile Awards , and Screaming Mi Mi Awards .

collections.title: Hillside Orchard Farms
collections.description: Hillside Orchard Farms is a celebrated family-owned farm and food producer based in Tiger, Georgia . While they focus on flavor, they do produce high-heat sauces utilizing Ghost Peppers and Habanero Peppers , often balancing them with a savory garlic or fruit base to keep them "culinary" rather than just painful. They avoid the "chemical" aftertaste common in mass-market sauces. Because they are a farm first and a manufacturer second, their products taste like the harvest.

collections.title: Honey Sauces
collections.description: Honey is the "velvet glove" covering the "iron fist" of a high-heat sauce. While white sugar provides a flat, clinical sweetness, honey offers a complex, floral, and viscous profile that transforms a sharp burn into a luxurious glow. Honey is a supersaturated solution of fructose and glucose. Like with other fruits, these sugars are the primary biological distraction for capsaicin.

collections.title: Hook And Arrow Sauces
collections.description: Hook & Arrow is a Connecticut-based company founded by brothers Sam and Henry. Their brand is heavily influenced by their upbringing in the outdoors—specifically fishing, hiking, and camping—and they position their sauces as the "perfect addition to your next adventure." They are strictly "all-natural," meaning they don't use artificial thickeners (like xanthan gum) or preservatives. Because of this, their sauces naturally separate, and they encourage a "shake well" approach. They donate a portion of their profits to organizations focused on protecting public lands, waterways, and wildlife.

collections.title: Hot N Saucy
collections.description:
Chef-Driven Craft: Hot N Saucy is a Black-owned and woman-owned brand founded in Long Island City, Queens, New York , by professional chef Samantha Evans .

 Culinary-First Philosophy: Created to disrupt ordinary, vinegar-heavy sauces, the brand focuses on bold vegetable bases and bright, complex flavor profiles where heat enhances the food rather than overpowering it.

 Small-Batch Quality: Every bottle is made in New York using all-natural, gluten-free, and vegan ingredients , balancing fiery chiles with fresh produce for a gourmet, craveable finish.

collections.title: Hot Sauces
collections.description: Ready to turn up the volume? Our Hot selection strikes the perfect equilibrium between intense heat and vibrant flavor. These aren't just additives; they are center-stage ingredients that bring a fiery personality to wings, pizza, and marinades. Expect a sharp bite followed by a satisfying, full-bodied heat.

collections.title: Hottest Sauces
collections.description: You’ve officially reached the peak of Scoville Mountain. This collection is reserved for the elite—the seasoned professionals who eat fire for breakfast. Featuring pure pepper extracts and the world's most lethal chilis, these sauces demand respect. Use with extreme caution: a single drop is often all you need to transform an entire pot of chili into a volcanic experience. Proceed only if you dare.

collections.title: HYCH: Heat You Can Handle
collections.description: HYCH (Heat You Can Handle) is a craft hot sauce company founded on the principle that hot sauce should be an everyday condiment rather than a dare. Based in Nashville, Tennessee , the brand was created by Will Collier , a hot sauce enthusiast who was frustrated by the "arms race" of extreme heat that often sacrificed flavor for pain. HYCH focuses on "culinary-forward" sauces that prioritize a balanced, food-friendly experience, making them accessible to both casual diners and hardcore chili-heads.

collections.title: Items On Sale
collections.description: It's time to save some money through some great deals!

collections.title: Jalapeno Pepper
collections.description: If the world of hot sauce had a "Greatest Hits" album, the Jalapeño would be the opening track. While it may not have the face-melting intensity of a Ghost Pepper or the trendy status of the Habanero, it remains the undisputed backbone of the hot sauce industry. Unlike many super-hot peppers that lean into floral or fruity notes, the jalapeño is prized for its vegetal quality. On the Scoville Scale, jalapeños are the gold standard for "medium" heat. They provide a pleasant tingle without ruinous pain, with 2,500 - 8,000 SHU.

collections.title: Karma Sauce
collections.description: Karma Sauce is an award-winning, farm-to-bottle hot sauce company based in Rochester, New York . Founded by Gene Olczak , a designer and engineer with a passion for flavor chemistry, the company is widely considered one of the most sophisticated "flavor-architect" brands in the world. Karma Sauce is unique because they grow the vast majority of their own peppers on their own farm, ensuring total control over the quality and ripeness of their ingredients. Karma Sauce is one of the most decorated brands in the industry, consistently sweeping the Scovie Awards and the NYC Hot Sauce Expo "Screaming Mi Mi" Awards . They have won "Best of Show" multiple times, a feat rarely achieved by such a small, family-run operation.

collections.title: Keto
collections.description: Stay in ketosis with our Keto-friendly sauces, seasonings, and condiments. We’ve eliminated hidden sugars and cornstarch fillers, replacing them with clean, vinegar-based heat and savory spices. Ideal for high-protein meal prep and grilled meats , these low-carb essentials ensure you never have to choose between your macros and your flavor. Bold heat, zero sugar, pure performance.

collections.title: La Nova Wings, LLC
collections.description: La Nova Wings, LLC is a legendary name in the "Wing Capital of the World," operating as the wholesale and distribution arm of the world-famous La Nova Pizzeria in Buffalo, New York . Founded by the Todaro family in 1957, La Nova is often cited as the largest independent pizzeria in the United States and is credited with being the first company to successfully "export" the authentic Buffalo wing experience on a massive scale. La Nova popularized the style of "double-dipped" or "char-grilled" wings. Their sauces are designed to be thick enough to glaze the wing, creating a sticky, caramelized coating that stays on the chicken rather than dripping off. They are the "official wing" of numerous NFL and MLB stadiums, proving that their sauce chemistry is stable and delicious even when produced in massive quantities.

collections.title: Lemon
collections.description: Adding lemon to hot sauce is a total game-changer. While lime is the traditional go-to for Mexican-style salsas, lemon brings a bright, floral, and slightly "sunny" acidity that pairs beautifully with garlic, herbs, and Mediterranean or coastal flavors. If you’re looking to brighten up your palate without just dousing everything in vinegar, hot sauces with some kind of lemon in them is the way to go.

collections.title: Lime
collections.description: If you’re looking to brighten up your plate, lime-infused hot sauces are the ultimate cheat code. While traditional hot sauces rely heavily on vinegar for that "zing," lime-based sauces offer a floral, citrusy acidity that cuts through fat and rounds out the heat of the peppers. Think of it as the difference between a sharp "sting" (vinegar) and a bright "zest" (lime).

collections.title: Limo Chili Peppers
collections.description: When it comes to Peruvian cuisine, the Aji Limo (or Limo Chili) is the undisputed crown jewel of heat. While the world often obsessses over the Jalapeño or the Habanero, the Limo offers a sophisticated, citrus-forward profile that elevates a hot sauce from a mere "burn" to a gourmet experience. Historically rooted in the north coast of Peru, these peppers belong to the Capsicum chinense species—the same family as the habanero—but they swap the heavy floral notes for a bright, crisp acidity.

collections.title: Little Dick's
collections.description: Little Dick’s is a bold, "no-nonsense" hot sauce brand that leans into a humorous, tongue-in-cheek aesthetic while delivering serious, high-quality flavor. The company’s identity is built on the concept of "Big Flavor, Little Bottle." They embrace the playful side of the hot sauce world—a community known for puns and "outlaw" branding—but prioritize the quality of the peppers above all else. In the hot sauce world, Little Dick’s is viewed as a "fun" brand that actually delivers. While some "novelty" sauces are known for being poor quality, Little Dick’s has survived for years because the product itself is reliable and tasty.

collections.title: Lucky Snipe, LLC
collections.description: Lucky Snipe, LLC is a boutique hot sauce and specialty food company deeply embedded in the Western New York (Buffalo/Niagara) culinary scene. Named after a "snipe"—a bird known for being difficult to hunt (hence a "lucky" find)—the brand positions itself as a premium, artisan alternative to the mass-produced sauces that dominate the Buffalo region. They prioritize fresh, high-quality ingredients over industrial fillers. You can often see the texture of the peppers and spices in the sauce, rather than it being a translucent, watery liquid. In the local Buffalo community, Lucky Snipe is viewed as a "Gourmet Table Sauce." While a cheap gallon of Frank's is for the mass-production of wings, a bottle of Lucky Snipe is what you put on the table for guests or give as a gift to show off the "modern" side of Buffalo’s spicy heritage.

collections.title: Mango
collections.description: The marriage of mango and chili peppers is a classic in the hot sauce world for a reason. Mango provides a thick, syrupy body and a natural sweetness that acts as a fire retardant, rounding out the sharp sting of high-heat peppers. The natural sugars in mango help neutralize the perceived burn of the capsaicin, allowing you to taste the fruit's profile before the heat kicks in. While mangos are sweet, they also have a bright acidity that complements the fermentation or vinegar used in the bottling process.

collections.title: Mark's Hot Sauces
collections.description: Mark’s Hot Sauce is an artisanal, small-batch craft hot sauce company based out of Montreal, Quebec . Founded in 2014 by Mark Cregan, the brand has grown from a local restaurant favorite into an internationally distributed name with a reputation for culinary-forward, fermentation-focused flavors. They apply an "Italian mentality" to their products—focusing on simplicity, clean profiles, and high-quality ingredients where less is more.   All sauces are free from artificial colorings or chemical preservatives, and the core lineup is vegan-friendly.

collections.title: Matador Mexican Grill
collections.description: Matador Mexican Grill , a popular "Fresh-Mex" destination in Fort Collins, Colorado , is famous for its legendary hot sauce bar . In the Northern Colorado food scene, Matador is often cited as having the best hot sauce selection of any fast-casual Mexican restaurant . Because they are made in-house at the restaurant, the sauces lack the "processed" vinegar-heavy taste of many commercial brands. You can taste the roasted vegetables and fresh herbs. They are respected for not "dumbing down" the heat—their hot sauces are genuinely hot, even by chili-head standards.

collections.title: Medium Sauces
collections.description: Our medium sauces are designed for the "everyday" heat seeker. These blends provide a noticeable kick that wakes up your palate without overstaying its welcome. If you're looking for a respectable simmer that still lets the flavor of your food shine through, you’ve found your sweet spot.

collections.title: Mighty Taco
collections.description: Mighty Taco is a legendary fast-food institution based in Buffalo, New York . Founded in 1973 by Dan Sacha, James "Jim" Sacha, and Bruce Sacha, it has grown from a single storefront on Hertel Avenue into a cultural icon of the Western New York region. What makes Mighty Taco sauces unique is their smooth, consistency and heavy spice-forward (rather than heat-forward) approach. They are often described as having a "deeply savory, taco-truck" vibe that focuses on the aromatics of the Southwestern spice rack. Mighty Taco sauces don't try to be "authentic Mexican." They represent a very specific 1970s-era "Americanized" taco style that is heavy on chili powder, cumin, and garlic .

collections.title: Mild Sauces
collections.description: Our Mild collection is proof that you don't need a massive burn to have massive flavor. Perfect for beginners and families, these sauces focus on tangy, sweet, and savory profiles with just a hint of "zip." It’s all of the taste with none of the pain.

collections.title: Murder Hornet
collections.description: Murder Hornet Hot Sauce is a small-batch, artisanal hot sauce brand based out of West Seattle, Washington. Known for its eye-catching branding and emphasis on robust, texture-heavy flavor profiles, the company has built a dedicated following by balancing high-quality regional ingredients with a distinct creative flair. Unlike many novelty brands with aggressive names, Murder Hornet focuses heavily on a "flavor-first, heat-second" philosophy. Their sauces use no artificial preservatives, thickeners, or added sugars, opting instead to fire-roast fresh, local produce in small batches to build natural caramelization, smoke, and emulsified thickness (they purposefully avoid using water as a main filler so the sauce clings to food instead of pooling on the plate).

collections.title: Murph's Style Wing Sauce
collections.description: Murph’s Famous Gourmet Wing Sauce is a legendary "Western New York" staple that represents the authentic taste of the Buffalo and Rochester corridor. Originating in Brockport, New York (just west of Rochester), the sauce was created by "Murph" (Mark Murphy) and was a fixture of his local restaurant before becoming a bottled retail sensation. It is widely considered the "gold standard" for those who want a true, restaurant-quality Buffalo wing at home.

collections.title: Newest Items
collections.description: Our newest collection of sauces has officially hit the site, featuring a curated lineup of blends designed for flavor-seekers. From tangy, fermented habanero arrivals to heavy-hitting Pepper X, extracts and reapers that demand respect, we’ve sourced the best new sauces to upgrade your pantry. Whether you’re looking for a smoky daily driver or a fruit-forward scorcher, these selections prove that real heat is an art form.

collections.title: Non-GMO Items
collections.description: Experience flavor the way nature intended with our Non-GMO sauces and condiments . We prioritize integrity by sourcing products crafted from ingredients free of bioengineering. From heirloom-quality peppers to natural, sun-dried spices, these seasonings and glazes offer a pure, authentic taste profile. Support sustainable farming and enjoy a cleaner, more vibrant culinary experience from the seed to your plate.

collections.title: Old Pueblo Poblano
collections.description: Old Pueblo Poblano is an artisanal hot sauce brand deeply rooted in the culinary traditions of Tucson, Arizona (historically known as the "Old Pueblo"). The brand is celebrated for capturing the smoky, sun-drenched flavors of the Sonoran Desert, specifically by highlighting the versatile and earthy Poblano pepper . Unlike many hot sauce brands that rush toward extreme heat, Old Pueblo Poblano focuses on the "slow" development of flavor. They are highly respected for their clean labels, using real ingredients without thickeners or artificial coloring.

collections.title: Onions
collections.description: Onions are the unsung heroes of the sauce and spice world. While chilis get the glory for heat and smoke, onions provide the aromatic structure that keeps a sauce from tasting "thin" or one-dimensional.

collections.title: Organic
collections.description: Experience the purest form of heat with our Organic collection . From pesticide-free hot sauces and rich BBQ glazes to natural seasonings, every product is crafted with certified organic ingredients . No synthetic additives—just soil-to-bottle integrity that highlights the vibrant, clean flavors of nature’s best peppers and spices.

collections.title: Package Deals
collections.description: Get a great value for a lower price with our package deals.  3 or more bottles for less money than if you were to purchase the bottles individually.  Buy more and save more today! Additional Discounts do NOT apply to package deals.

collections.title: Paleo
collections.description: Return to basics with our Paleo-approved collection. They’ve stripped away refined sugars, soy, grains, and artificial thickeners to bring you a clean standard of heat. Featuring fire-roasted peppers, organic vinegars, and whole-food spices , our sauces and seasonings add primal depth to your kitchen. It’s the ultimate clean-label fuel for grass-fed meats and roasted garden harvests —exactly as nature intended.

collections.title: Papaya
collections.description: Papaya is the unsung hero of the hot sauce world. While many tropical sauces lean heavily on pineapple or mango, papaya offers a unique, creamy texture and a subtle musky sweetness that acts as a perfect foil for high-heat peppers like Habaneros and Scotch Bonnets. Its natural enzymes (specifically papain ) also help mellow out the sharp "sting" of vinegar-heavy sauces, resulting in a smoother, more rounded flavor profile.

collections.title: Paprika
collections.description: Paprika is the unsung hero of the hot sauce world. While peppers like Habaneros or Ghost peppers bring the "fire," paprika provides the foundation, color, and soul . In hot sauce formulation, paprika is rarely the primary source of heat—since most paprika measures under 500 Scoville Heat Units (SHU) —but it is essential for creating a rich, savory profile.

collections.title: Passion Fruit
collections.description: Passion fruit is the "electric" ingredient of the hot sauce world. It is a high-vibrancy, high-acid fruit that provides a tropical "punch" that can cut through even the most aggressive super-hot peppers. In a kitchen where the savory weight is carried entirely by Garlic , passion fruit acts as the bright, aromatic counter-force. Passion fruit is unique because it is one of the few fruits that is more acidic than it is sweet. Most hot sauces rely on vinegar for shelf stability and tang. Passion fruit provides a natural alternative (or supplement).

collections.title: Peaches
collections.description: Blending the lush, sun-ripened sweetness of peaches with the searing heat of chili peppers is a culinary masterstroke. While many fruit-based sauces lean on mango or pineapple, peach-based hot sauces offer a unique, velvety texture and a floral aroma that bridges the gap between "savory" and "dessert" perfectly. The magic of this pairing lies in balance . Peaches contain natural sugars and a subtle acidity that act as a buffer for intense capsaicin. When you hit a high-heat pepper like a Habanero or a Scotch Bonnet against a soft peach base, the fruit tames the initial sting and allows the complex, fruity notes of the pepper to shine through.

collections.title: Pears
collections.description: When most people think of hot sauce, they picture fire-breathing peppers and sharp vinegar. However, the modern craft sauce movement has embraced a more sophisticated player: the Pear. Adding pears to hot sauce isn't just about making it "fruitier." It’s a strategic culinary move that balances heat with a unique, grainy texture and a floral sweetness that you just don't get from peaches or pineapples.

collections.title: Pepper Extract
collections.description: Whether you’re a casual fan of the "green bottle" jalapeño sauce or a seasoned heat-seeker who keeps a gallon of Carolina Reaper mash in the fridge, you’ve likely encountered the polarizing world of pepper extract . In the hot sauce industry, extract is the "nuclear option." It’s the difference between a sauce that tastes like a garden-fresh vegetable and one that feels like a chemical burn on a dare.

collections.title: Pepper X
collections.description: Since its crowning as the world’s hottest pepper by Guinness World Records in late 2023, Pepper X has moved from a mythical "Hot Ones" exclusive to the star of a growing lineup of extreme sauces. Bred by Ed Currie of PuckerButt Pepper Company, it averages 2.69 million Scoville Heat Units (SHU) . Unlike the Carolina Reaper , which delivers a "stinging" heat that hits the back of the throat, Pepper X is known for a "creeping" heat . It often tastes surprisingly sweet and floral at first, but once the capsaicin binds to your receptors, the burn can last for 20 minutes or longer, often affecting the entire mouth and chest.

collections.title: Peri Peri
collections.description: At its heart, Peri Peri (also known as Piri Piri or Pili Pili ) is the Swahili name for the African Bird’s Eye Chili . While the pepper itself is indigenous to Africa, the sauce is a beautiful historical accident—a fusion of African ingredients and Portuguese flair. Unlike sauces that rely on vinegar or heavy fermentation, a true Peri Peri sauce is defined by its bright, herbaceous, and citrusy profile . It’s less about a "burn" that ruins your palate and more about a "zing" that wakes it up.

collections.title: Pineapple
collections.description: Pineapple isn't just for pizza or poolside cocktails. In the world of hot sauce, it is one of the most versatile "bridge" ingredients available. Whether you’re a fan of a slow-burning habanero blend or a face-melting Carolina Reaper concoction, pineapple plays a crucial role in balancing the heat.  Pineapple contains citric and malic acids, which provide a bright tang. More importantly, it contains bromelain , an enzyme that breaks down proteins. While this is mostly neutralized during the cooking/bottling process, it helps create a smoother texture in the mash.

collections.title: Poblano Pepper
collections.description: In the vibrant world of hot sauce, the Poblano pepper is the sophisticated middle ground. While habaneros bring the fire and bell peppers bring the crunch, the Poblano offers a deep, soulful complexity that focuses more on flavor profile than sheer capsaicin intensity.  Poblanos are the "umami" of the chili world. When used as a base for hot sauce, they provide a thick, luscious texture and a savory backbone that brighter, thinner peppers lack.

collections.title: Puckerbutt Pepper Company
collections.description: PuckerButt Pepper Company is a titan in the world of spicy food, legendary for being the birthplace of the world's hottest peppers. Based in Fort Mill, South Carolina , it was founded by "Smokin'" Ed Currie , a man whose name is synonymous with high-stakes pepper breeding and "record-breaking" heat. PuckerButt uses high-quality mashes and often high-percentage pepper content in their sauces. Ed's peppers are famous for "creeping" heat—sensations that start mild and build to an overwhelming, full-body burn. Produced in collaboration with HEATONIST for the show Hot Ones . The "Xperience" and "Thermageddon" versions feature Ed’s proprietary peppers and are the final hurdle for every celebrity guest.

collections.title: Quentin's Hot Sauce
collections.description: Born from a Nashville backyard in 2020, Quentin’s Sauce was created to bridge the gap between "backyard-barbecue friendly" and "chef-level clever." Founded by Andrew in honor of his grandfather—Dr. Quentin, a World War II veteran and long-time fire chief—the brand embodies a philosophy of living with bold, purposeful flavor. Unlike traditional hot sauces, this small-batch lineup redefines the condiment category by masterfully blending the tangy, nostalgic comfort of classic American mustard with the intense, creeping heat of premium Carolina Reaper peppers.

collections.title: Raspberries
collections.description: Raspberries aren't just there for the sugar; they bring a complex structural element to a blend. When people think of fruit in hot sauce, mango and pineapple usually hog the spotlight. However, raspberries are the secret weapon of the hot sauce world. They offer a sophisticated profile that balances sharp acidity with a deep, floral sweetness that tropical fruits just can't replicate.

collections.title: Rising Smoke Sauceworks
collections.description: Rising Smoke Sauceworks is an award-winning craft hot sauce company based in Efland, North Carolina . Founded by Mike and Shannon "The Boss" Gilson , the brand has rapidly become a heavy hitter in the "flavor-first" spicy food community. Their hallmark is the use of smoked and roasted ingredients , which gives their sauces a signature depth that mimics the experience of high-end BBQ or wood-fired cooking. Rising Smoke is one of the most decorated brands in the modern era of hot sauce. They have won a staggering number of Scovie Awards , ZestFest Golden Chile Awards , and NYC Hot Sauce Expo "Screaming Mi Mi" Awards . They are widely respected by "Chili-heads" for their consistency and for being genuinely nice people in the industry.

collections.title: RJ's Gourmet Sauces
collections.description: RJ’s Gourmet Hot Sauces is a locally beloved, small-batch hot sauce company based in Rochester, New York . Known for its grassroots presence at regional festivals and farmers' markets, the brand focuses on the "Northwestern New York" style of sauce-making—which often emphasizes savory depth, garlic, and a thickness that is perfect for the region's famous chicken wings. Every bottle is produced in limited quantities to ensure the freshness of the peppers and the potency of the spices. While they are excellent on wings, RJ's markets their sauces as "all-purpose," designed to be used as marinades, dips, or even cocktail enhancers.

collections.title: Rocky's Hot Sauce
collections.description: Rocky’s Hot Sauce is a high-energy, artisanal hot sauce brand based in Long Island, New York . Founded by Rocky Gallo , the company was born out of a desire to move away from the "vinegar-water" consistency of traditional mass-market sauces. Rocky’s focuses on "Texture-Rich" sauces that act more like a thick pepper puree, ensuring that the sauce stays exactly where you put it—whether that's on a wing, a burger, or a slice of pizza. Rocky's has gained traction among the "Wing Enthusiast" community. Because the sauce is so thick, it is often used as a "finishing sauce" on dry-rubbed wings, adding a layer of moist, spicy texture that doesn't make the wings soggy.

collections.title: Rocoto Pepper
collections.description: If you’re looking to move beyond the usual suspects of jalapeños and habaneros, it’s time to get acquainted with the Rocoto pepper . Hailing from the Andean slopes of Peru and Bolivia, this pepper is a true outlier in the world of hot sauce, offering a profile that is as distinct as its high-altitude heritage.

collections.title: Rude Horses
collections.description: Rude Horses is an artisanal, family-owned hot sauce and gourmet food company proudly rooted in the Texas Gulf Coast region, operating out of the Greater Houston area. With their signature tagline, "The Flavor with Attitude," they have become a staple at regional Texas farmers' markets, pop-ups, and craft beer festivals. The sauce is purposefully crafted to be incredibly versatile—thick and well-balanced enough to be drizzled over grilled meats and tacos, used to elevate seafood, or swirled directly into marinades and dips.

collections.title: Sakari Farms
collections.description:
Rooted in Tradition: Sakari Farms is an Indigenous-owned and operated farm based in Tumalo, Oregon , founded by Inupiaq agriculturalist Spring Alaska Schreiner .

 From Seed to Bottle: Every bottle begins in the high desert soil, where heirloom peppers and ancestral First Foods are cultivated through regenerative, organic farming practices .

 Chef-Crafted Flavors: Developed alongside chef Sam Schreiner , each small-batch hot sauce highlights the natural fire, complexity, and distinct taste profiles of specialty tribal chiles .

collections.title: Sauce Crafters
collections.description: Sauce Crafters, Inc. is a legendary name in the hot sauce industry, known for producing some of the most iconic (and irreverently named) sauces on the market. Based in Riviera Beach, Florida , the company was founded by Charlie Schandelmayer , a pioneer who helped shape the modern "fiery foods" movement. They have won hundreds of Scovie Awards , Golden Chile Awards (at ZestFest), and Screaming Mi Mi Awards . In the community, they are viewed as a "Foundational Brand."

collections.title: Saucy Rebellion
collections.description: Saucy Rebellion is a craft hot sauce and condiment company based in Cedar Park, Texas (near Austin), that markets itself under the banner of a "Flavor Revolution." Founded with a rebellious spirit, the brand focuses on bold, creative flavor combinations that challenge the status quo of traditional condiments. They are known for their distinctively colorful branding, featuring gas masks and street-art-inspired graphics, signaling their intent to "disrupt" the boring pantry. In the Austin/Central Texas food scene, Saucy Rebellion is a rising star. They are a frequent presence at the Austin Chronicle Hot Sauce Festival and local farmers' markets. The brand has built a loyal following (the "Saucy Rebels") through social media engagement and a reputation for being one of the most approachable, fun-loving companies in the craft sauce world.

collections.title: Scorpion Pepper
collections.description: The Scorpion pepper averages around 1,200,000 Scoville Heat Units (SHU) , with high-end specimens peaking over 2,000,000 SHU . In a hot sauce, the Scorpion pepper acts as a "front-loaded" heat engine , providing an immediate, needle-like sting that forces the flavor profile to be built around high acidity or deep sweetness to balance its aggressive floral intensity. Unlike the slow-building Ghost Pepper, the Scorpion's high oil content ensures the heat coats the entire palate instantly, often allowing sauce makers to achieve extreme, "record-breaking" heat levels naturally without the metallic aftertaste of chemical capsaicin extracts.

collections.title: Scotch Bonnet Pepper
collections.description: The Scotch Bonnet Pepper is the undisputed "Sun King" of Caribbean cuisine. While other peppers are defined by their aggression or their smoke, the Scotch Bonnet is defined by its radiance. It is the essential ingredient in Jamaican Jerk and the soul of island-style hot sauces, offering a profile that is as much about tropical aromatics as it is about heat.

collections.title: Scoville Warming
collections.description: Scoville Warming is a boutique hot sauce company that focuses on the "science of the sear," providing sauces that emphasize a clean, progressive heat. Based on the concept of the Scoville scale, the brand is designed to help consumers navigate the world of spicy food through clear, tiered heat levels and transparent ingredient lists. They position themselves as a "Modern Culinary" brand, blending sleek, minimalist aesthetics with high-performance, kitchen-ready flavors. Scoville Warming has a reputation as a "Smart" hot sauce brand. They are favored by home cooks and professional chefs who appreciate their consistent heat levels and clean flavor profiles.

collections.title: Seasonings and Rubs
collections.description: Whether you’re aiming for a slow-burn brisket or wings that bite back, the secret to legendary BBQ starts long before the first drop of sauce hits the meat. While our hot sauces bring the finishing fire, our rubs and seasonings are engineered to build the foundation of flavor. From coarse-ground salts that lock in moisture to smoky chili blends that create that perfect, caramelized crust, these spices are the essential first step for any heat-seeker.

collections.title: Seed Ranch Co
collections.description: Seed Ranch Flavor Co. is a gourmet, plant-based condiment company based in Boulder, Colorado . Founded by David "DJ" Schwartz , the brand has become a leader in the "clean-label" movement, known for creating sophisticated, chef-driven sauces that prioritize organic, non-GMO ingredients. Seed Ranch is unique in the hot sauce world because they approach flavor like a high-end kitchen, utilizing "umami" ingredients and complex aromatics to create sauces that are as healthy as they are addictive. In the hot sauce community, Seed Ranch is respected for being "The Grown-Up Sauce." They are a perennial favorite at the Good Food Awards and have won multiple Scovie Awards for their innovation. They have also gained national recognition through Hot Ones , where their sauces have been featured for their ability to deliver complex flavor in the earlier "flavor-focused" slots of the show.

collections.title: Serrano Pepper
collections.description: The Serrano pepper is widely considered the "pro’s choice" for fresh Mexican sauces. If you’re looking for a sharp, electric heat that hits the front of the tongue and then gets out of the way, this is your candidate. It is sleek, bullet-shaped, and packs significantly more personality than your average supermarket chili. Between 10,000 and 23,000 Scoville Heat Units , it is roughly three to five times hotter than a standard mild chili. It provides a crisp "snap" of heat that enhances food rather than masking it.

collections.title: Shop By Brand
collections.description: Interested in a specific brand?  Everyone has their favorites, so we are making it easier for you to shop by individual brands so you can see if we have the brand you want and the sauce from that brand.

collections.title: Sinai Gourmet
